title: The Moon is our closest neighbour
description: Look out of the window at night. The Moon you can see through a small telescope is the closest thing to Earth in the whole of space — close enough that astronauts have stood on it.

body.heading: Not as far as it looks
paragraphs: The Moon looks tiny, like a coin in the sky. But it is really a big, round world made of rock. It is just very far away — so far that its light takes a whole second to reach your eyes.
Even so, it is our closest neighbour. People have flown there, landed, and walked on its dusty ground. No one has ever travelled to anywhere farther away.

body.heading: Mountains you can see
paragraphs: On a clear night, look at the Moon with a grown-up. The dark patches are flat, dusty plains. Long ago, people thought they looked like seas, and we still call them seas today — but there is no water in them at all.

Near the edge of the light part, you may spot bumpy shadows. Those are real mountains and craters, lit by the Sun from the side. The Moon has no weather, so its footprints and mountains stay just as they were left.

takeaway: The Moon is a big rock world and our closest neighbour in space — close enough that people have walked on it, and near enough to see its mountains from your window.
